note_en: 该 + verb + 的 turns an action into a noun phrase, "what should be [done]": 该省的一定要省 "what should be saved must be saved." It often comes in contrasting pairs: 该省的钱用在平时，该花的钱用在要紧时候 "the money to save is for ordinary days; the money to spend is for when it really matters." Here 的 stands in for an omitted noun ("what," "the money that").
